look_here_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: a cool-season winter ANNUAL with opposite heart/triangular SCALLOPED leaves, the upper ones CROWDED into a reddish-purple pointed top. Follow an UPPER leaf all the way to the stem: it retains a SHORT PETIOLE and DOES NOT form a stalkless collar. Henbit L. amplexicaule instead has rounded/lobed SESSILE upper leaves encircling the stem; both make pink-purple two-lipped flowers on square stems. Purple color varies with light/stage and is NOT diagnostic by itself.

key_traits.label: Life cycle
key_traits.text: Cool-season herbaceous winter annual with shallow roots and square stems often rooting at low nodes.

key_traits.label: Leaf arrangement
key_traits.text: Opposite at stem nodes, prominently crenate/scalloped; lower foliage broadly ovate/heart shaped and petiolate.

key_traits.label: Upper leaf
key_traits.text: Upper leaves short-stalked (PETIOLATE), crowded, more triangular/pointed, often distinctly purplish. Unlike henbit the bases don't form complete green stem-clasping collars; examine from below when top leaves overlap.

key_traits.label: Flowers
key_traits.text: Clusters (verticillasters) at upper nodes; pink-purple tubular two-lipped flowers, upper hood and patterned lower lip with pollen-bearing stamens.

key_traits.label: Stem
key_traits.text: Four-angled, often purplish near nodes; hairs can be sparse; cross-section is a mint FAMILY clue, not species-only proof.

key_traits.label: Fruits
key_traits.text: Four little nutlets develop within persistent calyx; mature nutlet/fruit macro not yet available.

key_traits.label: Habitat
key_traits.text: Disturbed winter-spring open ground, turf margins, beds, fields and paths; it is introduced and can provide nectar without constituting native host-plant support.
